about.subtitle: A little bit about who I am
about.bio_1: Computer Engineer with a background in electronics, specialized in backend development and cloud solutions architecture. At TeamWork Capacitación Ltda. in Santiago, I operate as technical lead and solutions architect — designing and building high-impact systems that power real operations.
about.bio_2: I lead two key initiatives: the Softland → Rex+ ERP migration (completed with zero data loss and zero downtime) and the Digital 24/7 Recruiter — an AI-powered mass recruitment agent on Azure serverless, with a cascaded multi-model pipeline (Claude, GPT-4o, Gemini) designed to process tens of thousands of applications during peak demand periods like Cyber Day.
about.bio_3: My engineering philosophy — "Augmented Engineering" — positions AI tools as technical capability multipliers, not replacements for sound engineering judgment. My path from electronics technician to cloud architect gives me a broad perspective that spans from low-level fundamentals to modern distributed systems.

teamwork.title: A system that grows with its people.
teamwork.intro: From an Excel-based process to a faster, more maintainable recruitment application. My challenge: evolve a prototype already running in production, from the data layer to the recruiters' experience.
teamwork.role: Backend development, database administration, and full-stack support for the frontend.
teamwork.diagram_note: Conceptual diagram of the components I worked on.

outcomes.title: Less waiting
outcomes.description: Optimized queries and heavy tasks moved into the background.

outcomes.title: More capacity
outcomes.description: Handling more people during periods of high demand.

outcomes.title: More visibility
outcomes.description: Monitoring to identify issues and improve proactively.

teamwork.story_title: The problem, the decisions, and the impact
teamwork.context: Recruitment and selection were managed through Excel files, causing information loss and inefficiencies. I joined when a functional prototype was already in production. I needed to address its shortcomings without breaking existing workflows. Azure Functions with TypeScript was new to me: I had to learn the ecosystem while analyzing the application end to end.

phases.title: Make the data coherent.
phases.description: The foundation was turning an inconsistent data model into a robust one, planning changes to preserve compatibility with the applications that consumed it.
points: Standardized table and column names and normalized the model to reduce redundancy.
Corrected data types, relationships, and unique keys to protect integrity and avoid duplicates.
Analyzed expensive queries and added indexes to improve response times.
Defined users, roles, and permissions per environment and application, and documented the model and standards.

phases.title: Build a maintainable backend.
phases.description: I refactored a codebase with mixed conventions and duplicated logic, making the responsibilities of each layer explicit.
points: Unified naming conventions in English, parameterized repeated logic, and removed unused code.
Implemented the repository pattern with dependency injection to centralize and abstract data access.
Added automated Jest tests to CI/CD pipelines and logging to monitor the backend.

phases.title: Decouple to grow.
phases.description: The architecture evolved so heavier processes would no longer block the recruiters' experience.
points: Moved file storage from an on-premise server to Azure Blob Storage.
Implemented queues for file processing and generation, emails, and synchronization.
Decoupled legacy-system and internal-ERP tasks to run in the background.

phases.title: Listen to the people using it.
phases.description: With a more stable foundation, we interviewed users to identify improvements to their daily work.
points: Implemented legacy-system synchronization and generation of occupational psychological tests and reports.
Automated monthly consolidation of strategic data to support management decisions.
New features addressed needs identified by recruiters.

teamwork.impact_title: A smoother operation. A more observable system.
teamwork.impact: The work streamlined recruitment, selection, and hiring, with shorter response times and the capacity to manage more people during demanding periods. Monitoring helped the IT team identify improvement opportunities, understand the most-used features, and act proactively. The result was a more manageable and maintainable application.

cyber.title: Apply once. Open more opportunities.
cyber.intro: I built an adaptable Cyber campaign website and an application system connected to the same ATS I evolved at TeamWork. Recruiters configure each opening, and people can apply again without starting over.
cyber.role: Development of the website and application system: ATS integration, server-side rate limiting, and document validation using OCR, Azure Document Intelligence, and OpenAI vision models.

outcomes.title: Less friction
outcomes.description: Reuse of existing data when applying to different openings.

outcomes.title: More traceability
outcomes.description: Application source and tracking by channel and campaign.

outcomes.title: Job fairs without manual transcription
outcomes.description: People apply on their phones by scanning the opening's QR code.

cyber.story_title: From scattered forms to a connected journey
cyber.context_title: When attracting candidates also meant losing information.
cyber.context: Campaigns were published in Canva, while applications relied on external Google and Microsoft forms. Search visibility was insufficient, and key data and documents lacked validation. Bulk submissions also triggered provider restrictions, interrupting applications during campaigns. The challenge was to support continuity throughout that journey and connect acquisition to the ATS.

phases.title: A website for more than one campaign.
phases.description: I developed a website the company can adapt to different hiring periods, instead of rebuilding an isolated presence for every event.
points: A reusable foundation for Cyber Day, Cyber Monday, Black Friday, and other campaigns.
An entry point to job opportunities and application forms.
An alternative to the previous Canva site, focused on improving presentation and digital presence.

phases.title: Forms that adapt to each opening.
phases.description: Recruitment staff can create forms for their needs, connected directly to the applicant tracking system (ATS).
points: Configuration of fields, required information, descriptions, and job openings.
Document uploads and validation of relevant data, such as identification and date of birth.
Checks that submitted information —including name, gender, or date of birth— matches the uploaded identity document.

phases.title: Protect submissions. Cross-check documents.
phases.description: I addressed two distinct problems: controlling form abuse and checking that declared details matched the identity document.
points: Implemented server-side rate limiting to limit abusive submissions.
Used OCR libraries, Azure Document Intelligence for identity documents, and OpenAI vision models with a fallback strategy.
Validation compares submitted details with the uploaded document, without depending on a single processing option.

phases.title: Apply again without starting again.
phases.description: I designed a journey that retrieves previously entered information when someone is interested in another opening.
points: Applicants review their existing data instead of filling out the entire form again.
They only add or update information specific to the new application, such as role or shift.
Applications are linked to the ATS, making them easier to track throughout the process.

phases.title: Understand where each application comes from.
phases.description: Diversifying and categorizing forms makes it possible to distinguish acquisition channels, both online and in person.
points: Identification of applications from social platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok.
Distinction between job portals such as Computrabajo, Trabajando, and Pandapé, and traffic from the Cyber website.
QR codes for job fairs: people scan and apply on their phones without depending on manual registration at the booth.

cyber.impact_title: A simpler application journey. More context for recruiters.
cyber.impact: The system made candidate acquisition easier, reduced repeated data entry, and helped retain application traceability throughout each hiring period. It also strengthened applicants' trust and simplified operations at job fairs. The solution continues to grow with recruitment needs.
